00003|  *
00004|  * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
00005|  * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
00006|  * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
00007|  * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
00008|  * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
00009|  *
00010|  * Dual mode:
00011|  *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
00012|  *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
00013|  *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
00014|  *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
00015|  *
00016|  * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
00017|  * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
00018|  */
00019| 
00020| import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

00022| import { dirname } from 'node:path';
00023| import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
00024| 
00025| /**
00026|  * Build the OpenCode CLI argument list.
00027|  *
00028|  *   - `run <prompt> --format json` is always emitted (`--format json` gives the
00029|  *     structured JSON event stream we parse for the transcript).
00030|  *   - `--model <extra.cliModel>` is appended when a model override is present.
00031|  *     cliModel is HOST-computed (resolveOpenCodeModel in agent.ts, threaded via
00032|  *     runnerExtra like codex's resolved model) so a canonical gateway id like
00033|  *     `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` arrives as `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` —
00034|  *     the form OpenCode routes through the configured `vercel` provider. There is
00035|  *     deliberately NO fallback to input.model: passing it verbatim is the exact
00036|  *     mis-route this fixes, and both runner entry points (the orchestrator and
00037|  *     the judge's eval-helper) always ship extra.
00038|  *   - else, when modelPolicy === 'native-default', `--print-logs --log-level INFO`
00039|  *     is appended so older OpenCode versions print the CLI-selected model (the
00040|  *     log-scrape path) without a follow-up export call.
00041|  *
00042|  * @param {{prompt:string, modelPolicy?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00043|  * @returns {string[]}
00044|  */
00045| export function buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input) {
00046|   const cliArgs = ['run', input.prompt, '--format', 'json'];
00047|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00048|   if (cliModel) {
00049|     cliArgs.push('--model', String(cliModel));
00050|   } else if (input.modelPolicy === 'native-default') {
00051|     cliArgs.push('--print-logs', '--log-level', 'INFO');

00061|  * `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` for a requested `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.

00063|  * that speak canonical gateway ids, and a gateway substitution still surfaces as

 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

00096|   if (!output || !output.trim()) {

00101|   // Filter to only include lines that look like JSON objects.

00144|  * Every emitted event carries a `sessionID` field.

00148|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00149|  */

00151|   if (!transcript) {
00152|     return undefined;
00153|   }
00154| 
00155|   for (const line of transcript.split('\n')) {

00169| /**

00171|  * Assistant messages carry `providerID` and `modelID` in their info.
00172|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.

00174|  * @param {string} exportOutput
00175|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00176|  */

00178|   const start = exportOutput.indexOf('{');
00179|   if (start === -1) {

00190|   const messages = parsed.messages;
00191|   if (!Array.isArray(messages)) {
00192|     return undefined;
00193|   }

00195|   for (const message of messages) {

00197|     if (info?.role !== 'assistant') {

00216|  * invocation, and we pass process.env straight through to the CLI. The runner
00217|  * never handles secrets itself.

00227|   // nothing else to do while the agent works. The sandbox-level timeout bounds it.

00246|   // include it, so first try scraping the printed logs (works on OpenCode <=

00248|   // messages carry providerID/modelID (OpenCode 1.17.0 changed the log format,

00252|     const sessionId = extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript ?? undefined);

00255|         const exportRes = spawnSync('opencode', ['export', sessionId], {
00256|           cwd: input.cwd,
00257|           env: process.env,
00258|           encoding: 'utf8',
00259|           maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00260|         });

00262|           observedModel = extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportRes.stdout || '');
00263|         }
00264|       } catch {
00265|         // Leave observedModel undefined.
00266|       }
00267|     }
00268|   }
00269|   const observedModelOrNull = normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) ?? null;
00270| 
00271|   if (res.error || agentExitCode !== 0) {
00272|     // Mirror the old error string: last 5 lines of output, else a coded fallback.
00273|     const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');
00274|     const fallback = res.error
00275|       ? `Failed to run opencode: ${res.error.message}`
00276|       : `OpenCode CLI exited with code ${agentExitCode}`;
00277|     return {
00278|       ok: false,
00279|       output,
00280|       transcript,
00281|       observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00282|       error: errorLines || fallback,
00283|       agentExitCode,
00284|     };
00285|   }
00286| 
00287|   return {
00288|     ok: true,
00289|     output,
00290|     transcript,
00291|     observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00292|     error: null,
00293|     agentExitCode,
00294|   };
00295| }

00297| /* ─────────────────────────── runnable (CLI) entry ─────────────────────────── */
00298| 
00299| // True when this file is executed directly (`node run.mjs ...`), false when imported.
00300| const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
00301| 
00302| if (isMain) {

00306|   // Always produce a RunnerResult, even if the runner itself throws, so the host
00307|   // always has a result file to read (node exit code stays 0 except on a truly
00308|   // unrecoverable crash before we can write).
00309|   let result;
00310|   try {
00311|     result = await runAgent(input);
00312|   } catch (e) {
00313|     result = {
00314|       ok: false,
00315|       output: '',
00316|       transcript: null,
00317|       observedModel: null,
00318|       error: e && e.message ? e.message : String(e),
00319|       agentExitCode: -1,

00321|   }

00324|   try {

00336|         observedModel: result.observedModel,
00337|         error: result.error,
00338|         agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
00339|       }) +
00340|       '\n'
00341|   );

00343|   // Exit 0: "the runner ran". Agent success/failure is conveyed via result.ok, not
00344|   // the node exit code (the host distinguishes the two).
00345|   process.exit(0);

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

00001| --- 00002| title: Prefetching 00003| description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js 00004| --- 00005| 00006| Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code. 00007| 00008| This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it: 00009| 00010| - [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work) 00011| - [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically) 00012| - [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching) 00013| - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) 00014| 00015| > **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path. 00016| 00017| ## How does prefetching work? 00018| 00019| When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route. 00020| 00021| Next.js automatically splits your application into smaller JavaScript chunks based on routes. Instead of loading all the code upfront like traditional SPAs, only the code needed for the current route is loaded. This reduces the initial load time while other parts of the app are loaded in the background. By the time you click the link, the resources for the new route have already been loaded into the browser cache. 00022| 00023| When navigating to the new page, there's no full page reload or browser loading spinner. Instead, Next.js performs a [client-side transition](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#client-side-transitions), making the page navigation feel instant. 00024| 00025| ## What Next.js prefetches automatically 00026| 00027| Next.js prefetches automatically in production. ---
title: Prefetching
description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
---

Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

---
title: Prefetching
description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
---

Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

---
title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch
description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns. ## Quick start Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear: ```ts filename="next.config.ts" import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption). If you'd like to enable everything, give your agent this prompt: ```prompt Adopt Cache Components and Partial Prefetching in this app so its navigations become instant. There is a Skill for each migration. 1. Before you change anything, explain to me in plain terms what Instant Navigation is and what adopting it will change. 2. Install the Skills you need, then verify your changes against a running dev server with next-dev-loop and agent-browser as you go: - next-cache-components-adoption: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption - next-partial-prefetching-adoption: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption - next-dev-loop: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-dev-loop 3. Each Skill leaves decisions to me, like how much of the work lands in each pull request. Put those questions to me and wait for my answers instead of deciding on my behalf. Adopt Cache Components first, then Partial Prefetching, following the workflow each Skill lays out. Don't rush to a passing build. 4. 00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. 00027| Install the skill:

00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```

00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:

00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.

00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. 00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```

00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.

00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |

00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |

00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. 00359| 
00360| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00361| 
00362| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00363| 
00364| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:
00365| 
00366| <FixCardGrid>
00367|   <FixCard
00368|     group="stream"
00369|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00370|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"

00375|     ]}

00378|     group="block"
00379|     title="Allow blocking route"
00380|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#allow-blocking-route"
00381|     snippets={[
00382|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00383|       { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
00384|     ]}
00385|   />
00386| </FixCardGrid>

00388| The insight never blocks the build, so this pass can happen any time after the flag is on. Load every route in `next dev` to check for it.

00394| export default async function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00395|   const { slug } = await params
00396|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00397|   return (
00398|     <ProductLayout>
00399|       <Details product={product} />
00400|     </ProductLayout>
00401|   )
00402| }
00403| ```
00404| 
00405| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher

00412|       <Details product={product} />
00413|     </ProductLayout>
00414|   )
00415| }
00416| ```

00420| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00421| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00422| 
00423| export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00424|   return (
00425|     <ProductLayout>
00426|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00427|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00428|       </Suspense>
00429|     </ProductLayout>
00430|   )
00431| }
00432| ```

00438|

00441|     <ProductLayout>
00442|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00443|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00444|       </Suspense>
00445|     </ProductLayout>

00447| }
00448| ```

00451| 
00452| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.tsx" switcher

00455| }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {

00460| ```

00470| Everything outside the boundary stays in the shared App Shell, and only the URL-specific region renders per navigation. Load or navigate to the route again to confirm the insight is gone and the page still paints meaningful UI.
00471| 
00472| > **Good to know**: A `params` or `searchParams` read inside [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) surfaces as [URL data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) instead.

00474| ## Prefetching URL data

00476| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching

related:

---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

00018|

00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```

00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |

00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.

00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. 00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.

00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. 00270| 
00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

00013| ---
00014| 
00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00016| 
00017| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00018| 
00019| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.

00098|   await page.goto('/products')

00175| ### Session content
00176| 
00177| Content behind [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) varies per session, not per link, and [session data resolves in the App Shell](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#include-session-data-in-the-shell), so cached session content still gets included. Read the session value outside the cached function and pass it in, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:

00182| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

00185|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00186|   const topics = await db.topics.forTeam(team)
00187|   return <TopicList topics={topics} />
00188| }
00189| 
00190| export default function Page() {
00191|   return (
00192|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00193|       <TeamTopics />
00194|     </Suspense>
00195|   )
00196| }
00197| ```
00198|

00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00270| 
00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00282| 
00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00288| 
00289| <FixCardGrid>
00290|   <FixCard
00291|     group="upgrade"
00292|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00293|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"

00302|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00303|     snippets={[
00304|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00305|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00306|       { text: '</Link>' },
00307|     ]}
00308|   />

00313| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00314| 
00315|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00316|    // Before
00317|    export default function Page() {
00318|      return <Dashboard />
00319|    }
00320|    ```
00321| 
00322|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00323|    // Before
00324|    export default function Page() {
00325|      return <Dashboard />
00326|    }
00327|    ```
00328| 
00329|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00330|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00331|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00332| 
00333|    export default function Page() {
00334|      return <Dashboard />
00335|    }
00336|    ```
00337| 
00338|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher

00340|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00341| 
00342|    export default function Page() {

00344|    }
00345|    ```
00346| 
00347|    > **Good to know**: If the page or layout already calls [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch), import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, so it doesn't collide with the `prefetch` export.
00348| 
00349| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00350| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).

00352| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:

00354| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00355| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app

00358| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00359| 
00360| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00361| 
00362| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00363| 
00364| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. 00366| <FixCardGrid>
00367|   <FixCard
00368|     group="stream"
00369|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"

---
title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about prefetching and instant navigations.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

--- title: prefetch nav_title: prefetch config description: Configure how a route segment is prefetched during client navigation. related: title: Next Steps description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice. links: - app/guides/instant-navigation - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant --- The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below. > **Good to know**: > > - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. > - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component. > - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly. > - A `page` or `layout` that also calls the [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) function needs to import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`. ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher export const prefetch = 'partial' export default function Page() { return
...
} ``` ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher export const prefetch = 'partial' export default function Page() { return
...
} ``` ## Options ### `'partial'` Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link. For links that opt into a wider prefetch with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), Next.js uses per-link prefetching. The server renders a fresh response that resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL). On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache. If a page accesses non-static data, it's prefetched at runtime. Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports. > **Good to know**: When Next.js performs a per-link prefetch for a segment, all downstream segments are included in the same request. Segments deeper in the tree that are configured with `'force-disabled'` will still be prefetched as part of the response. ```tsx filename="page.tsx" export const prefetch = 'partial' ``` ### `'force-disabled'` Never prefetch this segment. The client will not request segment data ahead of navigation. Use this for segments where prefetching would be wasteful, for example pages behind authentication that are rarely visited. > **Good to know**: `'force-disabled'` does not prevent Next.js from prefetching metadata about the route. 00013| 
00014| `partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.
00015| 
00016| ## Usage
00017| 
00018| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher
00019| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00020| 
00021| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00022|   cacheComponents: true,
00023|   partialPrefetching: true,
00024| }
00025| 
00026| export default nextConfig
00027| ```
00028| 
00029| ```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher
00030| module.exports = {
00031|   cacheComponents: true,
00032|   partialPrefetching: true,
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| `partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.
00037| 
00038| ## Reference
00039| 
00040| | Value   | Description                                                                                                            |
00041| | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00042| | `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app.                                                                            |
00043| | `false` | Keeps the previous prefetch behavior, for apps that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching was available. |
00044| 
00045| Leaving the option unset behaves like `false` and logs a warning when `cacheComponents` is enabled. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00046| 
00047| ## How prefetches resolve
00048| 
00049| Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.
00050| 
00051| With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.
00052| 
00053| The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.
00054| 
00055| > **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.
00056| 
00057| A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
00058| 
00059| > **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.
00060| 
00061| ## Per-segment overrides
00062| 
00063| A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.
00064| 
00065| ## Version History
00066| 
00067| | Version | Change                                                                     |
00068| | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00069| | 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |

00049| Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.
00050| 
00051| With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.
00052| 
00053| The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.
00054| 
00055| > **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.
00056| 
00057| A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
00058| 
00059| > **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.
00060| 
00061| ## Per-segment overrides
00062| 
00063| A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.

00068| | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00069| | 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |
00070|
